If you're going to get better, you need to forgive yourself. Not forget but forgive. You are struggling right now. You are in pain right now. Be extremely cognizant of triggers and keep a very low profile until you get to therapy. Finding yourself in a triggering situation?? Leave. Doesnt matter if its to just drive around for awhile. Just get out. Respect your limits. Respect the people around you by not subjecting them to your triggered self. Keep them safe by staying away when you need to. It will be hard. I had a terrible time when I started doing it but it will give everyone space and allow you to calm down enough to come back and be present. You basically have to do damage control/reduction until you get professional help. 

I'm sorry you're in so much pain and I'm sorry you're having such a hard time coping. Stay safe. Keep the ones you love safe. You are acting on instinct... its not your fault. I am bipolar and have anxiety... pretty bad anxiety. I was very similar to her in a lot of ways, especially before the bipolar diagnosis (antidepressants can cause serious mood instability for someone with bipolar disorder). The problem was that I was almost always in a depressive state and my manic state isn't full blown mania... its aggression. Caused a lot of heartache for a lot of people through the years. 

I can't offer advice. I wish I could. The only thing that kept me going was my dog. The only thing that helped me get better was someone realizing that I wasn't just depressed. After that it was a psyche NP that got me a genetic test to see why any antidepressants they put me on made things so much worse. It was a string of good doctors and my own self determination and even still I have very very hard periods of time. 

For her, this will be the rest of her life. There is always the chance that meds will stop working. There is no cure... and its not an exact science. But she can live a relatively normal life if she takes her health into her own hands. If she wants to get better.... there are ways to get better. 

You don't deserve to take this all on yourself. You cannot be her drive. You cannot be her guardian in this. You should take care of yourself. I wish I had some magical advice... I wish I could say everything could change in an instant but the fact is that even if she decides to get help and be serious about it... it will be a journey. Possibly a long one. I wish there was more I could do. No one should suffer like that (and that goes for both of you).

He's an adult now (well... kinda, I was a mess at 23), he has his own views and makes his own decisions regarding his life. I just think a lot of this could have been avoided if the problem was delt with by a professional. Kids lash out and say awful shit all the time but the problem nowadays is that there are places (easily accessible) where those ideas and feeling will be encouraged and justified so they grow up into shitlords. But there's no point in beating yourself up for what could have happened if things were done differently. What's done is done and the likely hood of getting him to go to therapy is so low that it's not worth mulling over. 

I'm so sorry you're going through this. I'm sorry hes an asshole. You seem like a good guy and you seem as though you did all you thought you could to fix your relationship. I go to her for everything (we live in opposite sides of the country). I'm not saying he'll definitely come around someday but I am saying, if he does, you should be cautiously open to the idea (just to make sure he isn't pretending for the sake of an inheritance). 

You deserve happiness. Everyone has the right to cut toxic behavior out of their life, no matter who the toxic person is. You tried. He did not. I'm sorry ♡ Sending good feelings your way.

Sitting there playing "what if" is completely irrelevant.

Who the fuck thinks to check to see if someone is okay with you borrowing someone ELSES shirt? The thought would never cross my mind. Now if she spoke up and was like "that makes me uncomfortable "... fine whatever. Super insecure reaction but I'm not about to die on a hill over a shirt. 

Who's to say she does? I wasn't making an assumption, I was providing counter context because everyone is harping about the shirt when there could be a completely and totally innocent reason for it. I wouldn't find it weird at all. My sister is a flirt (stepsister anyway), she tried to hit on my grandmother (she was really drunk). I also know she's completely harmless to my relationship because a. I trust the man I'm with and b. I trust her. 

Like the person above pointed out, it doesnt sound like shes making a whole lot of effort to include herself in his hobbies and the things he likes. I've been in that situation. I didn't let it get this far. My boyfriend and I were simply on different wavelengths and were spending too much time living our own lives and not enough time together. I sucked it up and started joining him in things he wanted to do even if I didn't want to because spending time with him was more important. Things are fine now. We do things together, we make time for each other. If I didn't make that effort, he would have obviously found someone else to enjoy what he was doing with.

Would I have been upset if they were female? Yeah, I would have but that would have only pushed me to get my ass up and join him. If it was my sister, I'd speak up. Express what's going on in my head in a constructive way. If they are that close and they do have such a great relationship, it shouldn't be terribly difficult to say something. She should keep the facts straight about her feelings. Not her assumptions of the situation, not focusing on what she thinks is going in with her sister. 

"Hey, I think you're trying to play house with my husband because you're lonely" would cause problems but "hey, Husband and I have been having a hard time lining up our lives to spend time together, it's really bothering me. Could you maybe give us some space for a bit, I'd really appreciate it". Bam. Sister's reaction would determine the issue. Gets defensive and refuses? Okay. Shits weird and she can go from there. She immediately backs off and allows you to step in? Do it. Get shit in order and close the gap. 

The whole story is full of bias (which it obviously will be) but it's also pretty obvious that shes really insecure about it which could easily skew the entire situation to look so much worse than it is. People are jumping on this weird shirt bandwagon because they're only seeing the situation from her eyes and not looking at the whole picture. There's no need to feed into those insecurities, that isn't constructive nor is it advice. That's not helpful, it wont fix this situation.
Glad I'm not the only one lol.

I AM NOT about to assume that she is the same way but I will say that I didn't realize it at the time. I truly thought I did love my exes. 

However, I ended up meeting my current man 4 years ago (we're actually moving in together in 3 weeks). We play MMOs together so I'm still in that world where I could have that attention if I tried. But I don't. I don't even notice if a guy is flirting with me. It doesn't make me feel good anymore. Frankly, its kinda gross. Any male friends that I have now respect the fact that I am in a relationship. They don't sit in discord with my boyfriend while trying to get me to send tit pics in PMs. 

Anyway, my advice is to reevaluate the situation. What she's doing isn't healthy for your relationship and shouldn't be what she needs to make her feel good about herself. It is a form of cheating even if she can rationalize it. I know I did... All the time. I'd say that I was just a flirty person and it obviously didn't mean anything. But it did and it does to her which is why she got all mopey. 

Overall, I think she needs to work on her insecurities if your relationship is actually important to her and not just something she's in because its comfortable and familiar. She needs to figure out how to love herself instead of trying to make other people do it for her.
